cases.reply:
Found it: `LRU.Set` released the mutex before calling `evict()`, so two concurrent `Set` calls could both see `len(c.items) > c.max` and walk the list while another goroutine was pushing to it.

Moved `evict()` inside the lock in `LRU.Set` (with a `defer c.mu.Unlock()`). I ran `go test -race -run TestCacheEviction -count=20 ./internal/cache/` and it passed all 20 runs, so `TestCacheEviction` is no longer flaky.
